title: Tapestry of Black Britons at the Hastings Museum
venue: Hastings Museum & Art Gallery, Bohemia Road, Hastings
summary: Paula Ogun Hector's five large-scale woven artworks, telling the story of almost 2,000 years of African and Caribbean presence in Britain, run at Hastings Museum & Art Gallery until 8 November. Local embroiderers and Hastings Academy students have also created a modern Hastings Bayeux for the exhibition. Entry and parking are free.

title: Nigel Kennedy at the De La Warr Pavilion
summary: The Rye International Jazz and Blues Festival presents an evening with violinist Nigel Kennedy at the De La Warr Pavilion on Friday 6 November, with a mix of classical, jazz and contemporary repertoire.

title: Reflections of a Night Sky at blackShed
summary: A free Dark Skies event on Friday 6 November about water and nocturnal creatures, with a short nocturnal walk, a telescope, and a talk on light pollution.

title: Bonfire Blazing at Powdermills
summary: A bonfire lit on the lake with a crafted effigy at its centre, plus live music, a hog roast and a whiskey bar, going ahead rain or shine with no fireworks.

title: Bonfire Blazing at Crafted at Powdermills
time: Gates open at 6pm; last orders at 10pm
venue: Crafted at Powdermills, Powdermill Lane, Battle
summary: A bonfire is lit on the lake with a crafted effigy at its centre, live music by the lake and a hog roast firing through the night. The organisers say there are no fireworks, out of respect for the wildlife on the grounds.

title: Dark Skies 2026: Reflections of a Night Sky
summary: A free evening celebrating moths, bats and nocturnal birds, with a short nocturnal walk, a collaborative textile activity, a talk on dark skies and light pollution, and a telescope to try out.

title: Veterans Hub social gathering
venue: The Veterans Hub, 45 Robertson Street, Hastings
summary: Open to all, after the 11am Remembrance Day service at the war memorial in Alexandra Park.

title: Rye Bonfire
summary: A torch-lit procession leaves Tilling Green and moves through the town, ending with a big bonfire on the Salts and fireworks, including a giant fire-breathing dragon called Scorch.

title: Robertsbridge Bonfire
summary: The town's procession moves through the High Street to end at the recreation ground, where a giant bonfire is lit and fireworks follow.
